title: Rework lazy activation and tokenizer prefetch pipeline to remove startup stalls
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: In production load tests and customer reports we've seen intermittent startup stalls when a model is first activated in a worker. Root causes observed: (1) synchronous weight shard deserialization that blocks main serving threads, (2) eager tokenizer initialization that allocates large vocab tables on the first request, and (3) blocking KV cache priming when cached prefixes are loaded on cold-start. Goal: Rework the activation pipeline so worker startup and first requests avoid tail-latency spikes while preserving memory safety and deterministic activation ordering. This ticket scopes a cross-cutting refactor: introduce an activation coordinator, convert heavyweight IO to cancellable background tasks, and introduce a tokenizer prefetch plan that warms smallest-needed artifacts first. This is a tech-debt cleanup (no API changes) but requires careful sequencing and integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start p95 per-token latency for first request reduced by at least 60% vs current baseline in our canary cluster
No increase in steady-state CPU or memory usage beyond 5% in dedicated instances after change
Activation coordinator supports cancellation and exposes activation state via /internal/activation-status for debugging
Tokenizer warmup is on a configurable critical-path threshold: default warms tokenization tables needed for first 512 tokens only
All existing unit and integration tests pass; new tests cover failure/retry during background deserialization
tasks: Design activation coordinator API and lifecycle (owner: Ravi)
Move weight shard deserialization to interruptible background worker with prioritized queue (owner: backend-team)
Implement tokenizer prefetch plan: quick-vocab vs full-vocab warm paths (owner: infra-team)
Add health endpoints + tracing hooks to observe activation progress (owner: observability)
Create integration test harness that simulates heavy model activate + simultaneous requests (owner: qa)
Rollout canary to staging, collect telemetry, then to 10% production, and finally full rollout after 72h validation (owner: release-engineering)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Background deserialization could leak memory if cancelled mid-way. Mitigation: use scoped allocators and ensure cleanup in cancellation path

Risk: Tokenizer partial warm may return slightly slower first tokens for rare long-prefix prompts. Mitigation: make prefetch threshold configurable and provide opt-in eager-warm flag for enterprise customers
Risk: Coordination introduces a new leader-election-style dependency across threads. Mitigation: keep coordinator per-worker (no cross-worker locking) and rely on existing process-level supervision
implementation_notes: Prefer async-friendly IO primitives already in runtime-io module; avoid adding new thread pools unless justified
Expose a feature flag runtime.activate_lazy_prefetch to gate rollout
Keep activation ordering deterministic: weights -> KV cache -> tokenizer minimal warm -> background full warm
